title: OwnMem review candidate
description: A lead offered to a person, never a memory. The schema is the gate every extractor has to pass -- deterministic today, host-assisted or model-backed later -- so that 'only schema-valid candidates exist' is enforced by the writer rather than promised by each producer. Everything a candidate may say is enumerated here: there is no free-text field, because a sentence in a review queue is one copy-paste away from being a memory.

candidate_id.description: Content hash of what the lead is about, not of the whole object. It has to stay the same as the observation grows, or a rejection could not stick across a re-scan.

lifecycle.description: Pinned. `candidate` is the one lifecycle with no path into a delivered context, and pinning it here means a producer cannot mint a lead that is already injectable.

logical_type.description: What kind of memory this lead might become, when it is a lead about writing one. A maintenance proposal does not propose writing a memory, so it carries null rather than a type that would be wrong.

observation.description: What the ledger or the corpus was seen to contain. One shape per kind, all closed: a producer cannot attach an extra field, and no field holds prose.

recalled_topics.description: Memories that were on screen while the observed thing was happening. Association only; the attribution field says how weak.

attribution.description: How the lead is connected to what it names. temporal_association: two things happened in the same window, and nothing here replayed the fix with the memory withheld. structural: the relationship is a property of the corpus itself (two topics really do declare the same document as authority and history), so no causal claim is involved at all. Neither is ever a contribution.

episode_id.description: The turn this came out of, or null when the producer works on something that belongs to no turn. Required-and-nullable rather than optional: 'nobody wrote it' and 'there genuinely is none' must not look the same.

session_id.description: The session this came out of, keyed, or null when the producer works outside any session. Null is not a pass: it is what makes the untrusted-context filter fall back to the coarser time window instead of letting the lead through unchecked.

policy.description: Restated on the object because the object is what a reviewer reads, and because a future caller must not have to infer it. All three are constants: there is no candidate for which any of them differs.

timestamp.description: Written as a pattern rather than format: date-time so this file validates under a bare ajv, with no format vocabulary the caller has to remember to register.

label.description: The gate name, or the allowlisted program name for a command. Never the command line.

identity.description: kind:fingerprint. For a command the fingerprint is keyed to this machine and reverses to nothing.

episodes.description: How many turns the red streak spanned, or null for a kind that belongs to no turn. Null is not zero: one means 'fixed inside the turn that broke it', null means unknowable.

label.description: The marker names, joined. Never the prompt: the classification is the whole record.

document.description: The doc_id one topic calls current authority and the other calls history. That disagreement is the whole finding.

members.description: [the topic that declares the supersede, the topic it retired and which is still active].
